context_label: Ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
title: Docetaxel every three weeks for recurrent ovarian, tubal or peritoneal cancer
schedule_label: One docetaxel infusion over one hour on day 1 of a 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain manageable.
schedule_summary: One docetaxel infusion over one hour on day 1 of a 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain manageable.
purpose: Docetaxel can slow the growth of epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer that has returned or is progressing. Your team reviews symptoms and scans with you to decide whether to continue.
indication_text: 00203e primary peritoneal, 00203f epithelial ovarian and 00203g fallopian tube cancer after relapse or progression. These uses are outside the Irish product licence.
administration_text: One docetaxel infusion over one hour on day 1 of a 21-day cycle. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain manageable.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver function. Blood count, kidney and liver function. Symptoms, examination and scans according to your treatment plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.explanation: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.
agents.watch: Take prescribed steroid premedication. Report fever, lasting numbness, swelling, sore nails or infusion symptoms.

Hair loss, mouth soreness and fatigue

support.title: Between visits
support.text: Call the 24-hour oncology number immediately for fever, chills, bleeding or feeling suddenly unwell. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, breathlessness, dizziness, throat tightness or pain at the infusion site.

teachback: Show which days you attend, which medicines you take beforehand and how to contact the 24-hour team.
consent_support: The prescriber will discuss the medicines on your individual plan. Discuss the possibility of persistent nerve symptoms, infection, hair loss and a severe infusion reaction.
safety_note: Call the 24-hour oncology number immediately for fever, chills, bleeding or feeling suddenly unwell. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, breathlessness, dizziness, throat tightness or pain at the infusion site.

evidence.title: Gynecologic Oncology Group phase II study
evidence.interpretation: Some participants with previously treated ovarian cancer had tumour shrinkage with docetaxel.
evidence.limitations: This was a small, single-arm study. It cannot show a survival advantage or establish the best dose or schedule for you.

additional_support: Docetaxel: dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice daily for 3 days starting the day before chemotherapy; at least 3 doses before the infusion. If missed, contact the team; any IV replacement is a consultant decision.
Reconcile the total dexamethasone schedule with antiemetics, including aprepitant interactions. The listed antiemetic steroid is a reference row, not an instruction to add a second course.
Assess G-CSF according to the exact regimen and individual risk.

Dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice daily for 3 days starting the day before docetaxel; at least 3 doses before treatment unless contraindicated. Missed doses require contact; 20 mg IV replacement is consultant-directed.
Reconcile the complete steroid plan with the antiemetic plan; do not add duplicate dexamethasone.
Low emetic risk: separate prevention/rescue medicines according to the national/local plan. Prophylactic G-CSF may be used after individual risk assessment.
